clean_body: - Michele Tafoya here! I never really considered running for office. Ever. I was too focused on raising my family, and being the best football sideline reporter I could be. But even in the last few weeks, Minnesota has become the embodiment of everything wrong with politics today. Tim Walz, his inner circle, and the corrupt political class are too busy: Wasting billions of our tax dollars on fraudulent daycares Failing to condemn the activists storming churches Raising prices on hardworking families Sabotaging anything the President wants to do Forcing men into women's spaces Pitting Americans against each other I can 't sit on the sidelines anymore. That's why I'm throwing my hat in the ring and announcing my candidacy for U.S. Senate! thought long and hard about the dynamics of this race before jumping in. Minnesota has long been considered simply out of reach for Republicans. The last time it voted for a GOP President was Nixon. The pundits and political experts say a Republican could never win here. But this year is going to be different for three key reasons: FIRST - I'm running against Tim Walz's right hand. All the rampant fraud that took place here happened under Peggy Flanagan's nose as much as it did under his. We will remind voters about that fact every single day. SECOND - The President has increased his voter share each time he has run. He nearly flipped this state in the last election, and Kamala Harris' running mate was our sitting Governor! Momentum is on our side. THIRD - I'm a different kind of candidate, and I know how to win. I didn't reach the top of my industry by pulling my punches. I put in the work. I never backed down. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. Hi again, human! 🐶
_WOOF!!_ It's me! **Bailey, the campaign dog**!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/60dd9c40-8fe7-4172-9b99-19ebf72bc63d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

In case you missed it, here's a bit about me: I'm a very good girl, big fan of trees (especially in the UP 🌲), a semi-professional napper, and the unofficial mascot of Team Haley.
My mom, Katelyn, is Haley Stevens' finance director, which means she spends a lot of time looking at screens and saying things like "Q1 projections." Blah blah blah - I JUST WANT PETS! 🐾 Sometimes, I gently remind her that belly rubs are just as important as fundraising goals. Self-care, mom!
Anyway - I've got my paw on the pulse of this campaign! And I'm here to share my dog-perspective of Haley Stevens for Michigan!
Coming to you LIVE, two feet from the ground and on all fours! 🦮 This is:
#### **A Campaign Dog 's-Eye View of Democracy**
You might think I spend all day chewing squeaky toys and chasing squirrels (yes, I do that too, and I have no regrets), but I also get to see what's happening out here on the campaign trail. I've been in the background on Zoom calls, sniffed at least 900 voters, and been in all the meetings (I'm excellent at going from person to person looking for pets). Here's what I've picked up:
🐾 **[Haley is loyal, scrappy, and loves Michiganders](https://substack.com/redirect/684dbd52-351a-48e5-a13f-733640e37fc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
** Just like me! But while my passion is stealing a sniff of my mom's Coney dog when she's looking at her phone, Haley is all about protecting Michigan jobs - she even helped lead the auto rescue way back in 2009. I've seen her prepping for speeches while eating lunch in the car, meeting with tons of voters at events all day, walking picket lines with unions, and still remembering to give me a treat when she gets back to HQ. That's dedication. And great snack awareness. (Honestly, an underrated quality in a senator, IMO.)
🐾 **[Michigan is one of the biggest Senate races in the country.](https://substack.com/redirect/684dbd52-351a-48e5-a13f-733640e37fc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
** Everyone's barking about it. This race is going to be close, and it's going to be tough - but us underdogs? We don't back down.
🐾 **[Haley has the best shot of any Democrat to win.](https://substack.com/redirect/684dbd52-351a-48e5-a13f-733640e37fc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
** That's not just me saying it (but I am biased because she always scratches my ears _juuuuust_ right). The polls say it too! Voters across Michigan know Haley is the best - she's from here, she's worked her tail off for working families, and she knows all the best spots for Detroit-style pizza! (BUDDYS! Yum.)
I love being a campaign dog. I get to be part of something hopeful and exciting, and I can see that humans are excited about Haley, too! I know this is going to be a tough race, but it is my official opinion that Haley Stevens would be an awesome senator.
So that's the paw-litical rundown!
There will be another update soon, but until then, I'll be doing my part - giving love to staffers and volunteers and reminding Haley about snacks and sitting patiently during long calls. 🐾
Thanks for following along! And if you see me out on the trail, come say hi! I love meeting Michiganders (especially the ones who smell like Coney dogs...)
XOXO,
Bailey 🐶
(_on behalf of my mom Katelyn, Haley, and the whole Team Haley pack)_
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

That’s 397 out of nearly 12,000 individuals who have had this honor and responsibility over the centuries.** Together, we’re fighting to make childcare affordable so no parent is forced to choose between a career and their family. We’re standing firm to preserve the rights to choose and codify reproductive freedoms once afforded by Roe v. Wade into federal law. And we remain focused on finally closing the wage gap and ensuring equal pay for equal work. My fellow Patriot,

Letter writing is such a lost art these days.

When I first joined the Marine Corps, nothing felt better than getting letters from loved ones.

And as I was looking back on that experience, I got the idea to write a letter to you.

You're so important to me - no, really.

If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have the incredible opportunity to serve our country that I have as Vice President.

Your opinion matters to me. That's why I want to personally invite you to take our America First Survey.

As the America First movement continues to take on new challenges, I need to know that we're best representing you.

Please, take our survey as soon as you can so I can see your responses.

It will only take five minutes, but it would mean the world to me.

Sincerely,

JD Vance

clean_body: I wanted to personally contact you. My fellow Patriot United States of America My fellow Patriot, Letter writing is such a lost art these days. When I first joined the Marine Corps, nothing felt better than getting letters from loved ones. And as I was looking back on that experience, I got the idea to write a letter to you. You're so important to me - no, really. If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have the incredible opportunity to serve our country that I have as Vice President. Your opinion matters to me. That's why I want to personally invite you to take our America First Survey. As the America First movement continues to take on new challenges, I need to know that we're best representing you. Please, take our survey as soon as you can so I can see your responses. It will only take five minutes, but it would mean the world to me. Sincerely, JD Vance Vice President of the United States of America Paid for by the Republican National Committee Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee.

body:
Sixteen years ago today, President Barack Obama signed the Affordable Care Act (ACA) into law. [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127918336/609641315/693975070?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MjEyYWJkNi0wNzI3LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gCiS_5Dl65NOey2mVEZCh5OPvVCbUv2ig-cWsWKXYaE=&emci=3b2bb202-f926-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=4212abd6-0727-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=15820338)
---

Peter,

Sixteen years ago today, President Barack Obama signed the Affordable Care Act (ACA) into law. As I watched this happen from back home in Washington, I breathed a sigh of relief. 40 million Americans were granted access to care that wasn't available to them before. People with pre-existing conditions–people like me–were protected. As a pediatrician, knowing my patients would be covered was incredible.

For far too long, I watched parents worry when they couldn't afford their child's medication. I saw parents delay a visit to the pediatrician because of expense. And there were too many patients to count who had a preexisting condition that insurance companies refused to cover–something that infuriated me as a woman living with type 1 diabetes. For these families, the Affordable Care Act wasn't just a relief, it was a lifeline.

**Yet, despite all the incredible good this piece of legislation did, and despite its overwhelming popularity, Republicans in Congress have been relentless ever since in their attempts to dismantle it.** In 2017, I joined three other doctors from my clinic to take action. We held an urgent meeting with our representative to explain how the ACA helped protect our patients–his constituents–and yet two days later, our congressman betrayed WA-08 and voted to overturn the ACA.

That vote was the final straw for me.

Sensing I could do more good for the children and families of Washington's 8th District from a seat in the House of Representatives than I ever could in the four walls of my exam room, I packed up my office and left the job I loved to run for Congress.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127918337/609641316/1210615431?refcode=em26_260323_aca_fndd_gq_act___DKS_ettx&&&&utm_campaign=em26_260323_aca_fndd_gq_act___DKS_ettx&&&&utm_medium=email&&&&refcode2=4212abd6-0727-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&refcode2=4212abd6-0727-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MjEyYWJkNi0wNzI3LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gCiS_5Dl65NOey2mVEZCh5OPvVCbUv2ig-cWsWKXYaE=)
Thanks to the support of this incredible team, we flipped WA-08 blue for the first time in history, and we've kept it blue ever since. And in Congress, I have fought consistently to improve healthcare affordability and accessibility. We gave Medicare the power to negotiate the cost of prescription drugs. And capped insulin at $35/month for seniors.

clean_body: Sixteen years ago today, President Barack Obama signed the Affordable Care Act (ACA) into law. Peter, Sixteen years ago today, President Barack Obama signed the Affordable Care Act (ACA) into law. As I watched this happen from back home in Washington, I breathed a sigh of relief. 40 million Americans were granted access to care that wasn't available to them before. People with pre-existing conditions–people like me–were protected. As a pediatrician, knowing my patients would be covered was incredible. For far too long, I watched parents worry when they couldn't afford their child's medication. I saw parents delay a visit to the pediatrician because of expense. And there were too many patients to count who had a preexisting condition that insurance companies refused to cover–something that infuriated me as a woman living with type 1 diabetes. For these families, the Affordable Care Act wasn't just a relief, it was a lifeline. Yet, despite all the incredible good this piece of legislation did, and despite its overwhelming popularity, Republicans in Congress have been relentless ever since in their attempts to dismantle it. In 2017, I joined three other doctors from my clinic to take action. We held an urgent meeting with our representative to explain how the ACA helped protect our patients–his constituents–and yet two days later, our congressman betrayed WA-08 and voted to overturn the ACA. That vote was the final straw for me. Sensing I could do more good for the children and families of Washington's 8th District from a seat in the House of Representatives than I ever could in the four walls of my exam room, I packed up my office and left the job I loved to run for Congress. = Thanks to the support of this incredible team, we flipped WA-08 blue for the first time in history, and we've kept it blue ever since. And in Congress, I have fought consistently to improve healthcare affordability and accessibility. We gave Medicare the power to negotiate the cost of prescription drugs. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Will you support the next Resistance Lab?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Organizing takes time, but it works when we do it together.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260323-6041-footer&t=1&akid=6041%2E420207%2E9Lpjxv)
Peter,
I say it all the time because it is true: **Action is the best antidote to hopelessness and powerlessness.**
Since Trump retook office, chaos has spread across the country. His administration's goal has been to overwhelm us, exhaust us, and make people feel like nothing they do can matter.
Hopelessness is _exactly_ what authoritarians count on. They want to convince us that nothing matters, that we are alone, that it is too late. But that is not true.
The truth is what you do _matters_.
**Every conversation you have, every protest you attend, every time you show up for your community, it creates ripple effects reaching farther than you can see.**
That is why I started the Resistance Lab — a series of grassroots trainings designed to turn fear, anger, and urgency into meaningful, nonviolent action so together we can fight back.
During my Resistance Labs trainings we bring people together to build skills, understand risk and strategy, connect across communities, and commit to concrete steps that defend our values.
But the Resistance Lab is not free to run. Each training costs about $10,000 in hard costs, not including staff time. I fund these trainings through my campaign because I believe this work is essential. But to keep scaling it, I need your help.
[**So if you can, will you pitch in $3 or any amount that works for you to help fund our next Resistance Lab and power this people-led movement?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260323.ECUk2v&refcode=em20260323-6041&amount=3&t=2&akid=6041%2E420207%2E9Lpjxv)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260323.ECUk2v&amount=3&refcode=em20260323-6041&t=21&akid=6041%2E420207%2E9Lpjxv)**
Thank you,
Pramila Jayapal
P.S. **[If you have not already, I hope you will sign up for our next virtual Resistance Lab training on May 3rd!](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/53320?t=22&akid=6041%2E420207%2E9Lpjxv)** We hope to see you there.
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260323-6041-footer&t=23&refcode2=6041_420207_9Lpjxv&akid=6041%2E420207%2E9Lpjxv)**

That's not MS Now. That's not a Democratic pollster. That's Fox News.

clean_body: - Michele Tafoya here! I never really considered running for office. Ever. I was too focused on raising my family, and being the best football sideline reporter I could be. But even in the last few weeks, Minnesota has become the embodiment of everything wrong with politics today. Tim Walz, his inner circle, and the corrupt political class are too busy: Wasting billions of our tax dollars on fraudulent daycares Failing to condemn the activists storming churches Raising prices on hardworking families Sabotaging anything the President wants to do Forcing men into women's spaces Pitting Americans against each other I can 't sit on the sidelines anymore. That's why I'm throwing my hat in the ring and announcing my candidacy for U.S. Senate! thought long and hard about the dynamics of this race before jumping in. Minnesota has long been considered simply out of reach for Republicans. The last time it voted for a GOP President was Nixon. The pundits and political experts say a Republican could never win here. But this year is going to be different for three key reasons: FIRST - I'm running against Tim Walz's right hand. All the rampant fraud that took place here happened under Peggy Flanagan's nose as much as it did under his. We will remind voters about that fact every single day. SECOND - The President has increased his voter share each time he has run. He nearly flipped this state in the last election, and Kamala Harris' running mate was our sitting Governor! Momentum is on our side. THIRD - I'm a different kind of candidate, and I know how to win. I didn't reach the top of my industry by pulling my punches. I put in the work. I never backed down. And I kept fighting, no matter what the naysayers said. In my years on the sidelines, I 've seen a LOT of underdogs win football games that the "experts" said were impossible. The Minnesota Senate race will be another chapter in that storied history. | | ---|--- Thanks in advance for your support. I'll never forget the good folks who stepped up in the opening days of this campaign. You and I are going to do great things together. I can feel it. Be brave. Do good. - Michele Michele Tafoya Republican for Senate, Minnesota It's official - Michele Tafoya is running for U.S. Senate in Minnesota! body:
Tax the rich
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260323-2643)
Peter,
When I talk about making the ultrawealthy pay their fair share, people often point out that Wisconsin only has 7 billionaires. That is, according to [Forbes](https://act.francescahong.com/go/6993?t=1&akid=2643%2E105371%2EeaFLGA).
Meet Joe Berrada, Milwaukee's biggest landlord and Wisconsin's newest billionaire. He didn't make the Forbes list, but [new reporting](https://act.francescahong.com/go/6994?t=2&akid=2643%2E105371%2EeaFLGA) from John Johnson, a Marquette Law School research fellow, revealed that Berrada recently disclosed a net worth exceeding $1 billion in federal securities filings.
In 2021, the Wisconsin Department of Justice sued his companies for charging tenants fees they didn't owe and confiscating renters' property. They settled for $1.7 million, the largest housing settlement in state history.
The following year, he filed 850 evictions in two weeks, overwhelming the Milwaukee County court system. When a tenants union raised safety concerns after a fire at one of his properties killed a young child, he sued them and lost.
This January, two of his buildings lost heat in the dead of winter, displacing dozens of tenants for two weeks. The fine for leaving people without heat in January? $365.76.
Nearly a third of Wisconsin residents are renters. I'm one of them. And as anyone who's ever rented in Wisconsin can attest, the system is built to protect landlords, not tenants.
As governor, I'll fight to ensure that every tenant facing eviction the right to a lawyer, give enforcement agencies the teeth to go after predatory landlords, and get the state out of the way so cities can pass rent control if their communities need it.
And, while we’re at it, we’ll tax billionaires like Berrada and invest in public infrastructure like universal childcare, paid leave for all, fully funded schools, and fairer, cheaper healthcare.
**[Are you ready to join the fight? Send us $5, and we’ll do the fighting for you.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260322.MBc5DN&refcode=em20260323-2643&t=3&akid=2643%2E105371%2EeaFLGA)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260322.MBc5DN&amount=5&refcode=em20260323-2643&t=22&akid=2643%2E105371%2EeaFLGA)**
Your working-class champion,
Fran

| | We’ve got some encouraging news to share — but also more reasons why we can’t take our feet off the gas. [**Keep reading to learn about how we’re combating specific threats to the freedom to vote in Mississippi and Georgia right now, and chip in to help grow our movement.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127919771/609646052/1173499294?refcode=emm_ffa_20260323_T1_LegUpdate_v1s1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NzY3ZjVlNy0wYzI3LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=e9JJCsEGsLa2pQTAxzZ1b-f1h1CURWXy_WAY2yiednE=) Earlier this month, we let you know about a key deadline in Georgia’s legislative session. Leading up to “Crossover Day,” we were racing to stop bills that would have...
* **Gutted our early voting system**
* **Deliberately tried to dilute Black political power in our most diverse counties**
* **Pushed Trump Regime propaganda and politicized access to voting**

If the bills didn’t pass one chamber by March 6, they couldn’t be considered by the other chamber in their current forms. With our team on the ground in the Georgia Capitol and working in close coordination with key allies, we were able to highlight the bills’ harms. And we successfully kept them from moving forward. Our fight is possible because of this grassroots team and your stalwart support. Thank you for everything you do. **But the Georgia Legislature is still in session through April 2, and ANY of those anti-voter provisions could get brought back in other pieces of legislation. We have to be ready to respond at a moment’s notice. With activists like you in the fight, that’s exactly what we’ll be able to do.** **And we face a critical threat in Mississippi, where extreme lawmakers are hurrying to pass a bill that would make it dramatically more difficult to register to vote, particularly for Mississippians living in rural communities, young Mississippians, and Mississippians with disabilities.** **Now we’re working with partners to directly reach out to Mississippi voters so they can contact their lawmakers in opposition to this legislation.** [**If you can power this pro-voter work with a donation today, it would go body:
# [#] Friends,

16 years ago today, the largest healthcare reform that our country has ever seen was passed.

Since then, the Affordable Care Act has been a lifeline for New Jersey. Because of it:

* Families have access to affordable plans
* Seniors are saving thousands on life-saving prescriptions
* Patients with pre-existing conditions can never be denied coverage again

But let’s be honest: that progress is under threat.

President Trump and extremists in Congress passed the largest Medicaid cuts in history — ripping care away from more than 12 million people. Jersey families deserve better. They deserve affordability and a healthcare system that works for them, not political chaos.

As a Problem Solver, I’m committed to bringing people together to protect what works and fix what doesn’t. That’s why I helped introduce CommonGround 2025, a bipartisan framework to extend ACA tax credits and lower premiums.

We’ve come too far to go backward. We must protect the ACA, strengthen its foundation, and continue building a system that puts patients first.

Will you add your name to help protect affordable healthcare? [https://go.josh4jersey.com/a/jg-aca]

PROTECT OUR HEALTHCARE >> [https://go.josh4jersey.com/a/jg-aca]

Thanks for stepping up,

Josh

He’s working across the aisle to find real solutions for New Jersey families and is actively fighting against the ideological gridlock in Washington. Our End-of-Quarter deadline is coming up fast, and we still have ground to make up.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127920261/609647333/1751931448?amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&amount=25&refcode=email_032326_path&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjVkNTcxYy0wZTI3LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Gtve-nYmzHuckoV-79Zb64foRJMolCLIP9qYnKCxMng=) **_Take our message directly to voters_**

It’s how we’ve already made real progress: repairing roads and bridges, investing in our public schools, cutting costs, and creating good-paying jobs right here in Pennsylvania. **_Keep delivering results_**
We’re going to win by continuing to prove that government can _actually_ work for people. Not through empty promises — but by doing the job. Getting things done and making a real difference in people’s lives. That’s the standard I've held myself to as Governor, and it’s exactly what I’ll keep fighting for. **_Build the kind of campaign it takes to win_**
We’re going to win by building a campaign that can continue competing everywhere — because in a state like Pennsylvania, we can’t afford to fall behind. Whether you’re chipping in, knocking on doors, making phone calls, or spreading the word, you’re helping to build the momentum this campaign needs to stand up to Donald Trump and his enablers, who are desperate to divide and distract from their own failures to deliver results. **_Crush every fundraising goal_**

It’s how we’ve already made real progress: repairing roads and bridges, investing in our public schools, cutting costs, and creating good-paying jobs right here in Pennsylvania. Keep delivering results We’re going to win by continuing to prove that government can actually work for people. Not through empty promises — but by doing the job. name: John Fetterman
subject: Can you help James out?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fetterman for PA
body:
---
Hey Derek, just wanted to make sure you saw my latest email:

James Talarico has a unique ability to reach across the aisle and get things done – for regular people, not ultrawealthy elites.
**That's why** **I'm hoping to raise another $5,000 by midnight to help James win this crucial Senate race. So I'm asking:****[Will you chip $5 or more now – split between me and James – to help us win in Texas and take back the Senate?](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53049?t=1&akid=10664%2E434096%2Es1qojE)**
Thanks Derek,

John

\---------------------- Forwarded Message ----------------------

| | | From: John Fetterman
Sent: Saturday, Mar. 7
Subject: James Talarico I’ll be direct, Derek:
---
Today, I’m asking you to split a donation of $5 between me and James Talarico – the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas. He’s building an unprecedented grassroots movement, and he needs our help. **[Will you chip in?](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53049?t=2&akid=10664%2E434096%2Es1qojE)**
| | [Donate](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53049?t=3&akid=10664%2E434096%2Es1qojE)
---
James is an eighth-generation Texan, a former middle school teacher, and a Presbyterian seminarian. He believes that the biggest divide in our country isn’t left vs. right – it’s top vs. bottom.
I couldn’t agree more. 💯
James knows what it takes to bring people together and fight for the working class and not the ultrawealthy and special interests, because he’s done it before. Now, he’s ready to keep up this critical work in the Senate, and I’m proud to support him.
Here’s the problem: The GOP and right-wing megadonors are already pouring in MILLIONS to try to crush his momentum, and unless we fight back now, we’ll lose our best chance to help Texas elect a Senator who *actually* cares about working people.
[**So please,****Derek****, have James’ back like you’ve always had mine. With Senate control on the line, will you split an urgent donation of $5 or more now to help us win in Texas and retake power for working people?**](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53049?t=4&akid=10664%2E434096%2Es1qojE)
Thank yinz,
John Fetterman 💙

I’m Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, a mom of three, and the Democrat running for U.S. Senate to defeat Republican Lindsey Graham in South Carolina.
If we flip this seat, we can end Lindsey Graham’s career and help Democrats retake the Senate, and expand the map for Democrats in future elections.
I know this won’t be easy. But I’ve treated kids who were shot, hospitalized, and failed by broken systems. Nothing about this moment feels optional.
We need an overwhelming surge of grassroots support to prove that we can finally defeat Lindsey Graham. So I’m humbly asking: Will you chip in a split donation of $50, $30, or even $15 between Resist Reclaim Rebuild and my campaign right now so we can hit our end of quarter goals? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews] [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
HELP ME DEFEAT LINDSEY GRAHAM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
Let me introduce myself.
I’ve spent nearly 20 years serving my community as a pediatrician, treating everything from asthma and violent trauma to the emotional toll of growing up in poverty.
I’ve seen what bad policy does to good families — and I’ve seen kids suffer because people like Lindsey Graham would rather protect their own power than protect children.
In 2022, after 15 years of working in hospitals, I ran for Congress because I knew our kids needed a voice in Washington. I lost — and I told my oldest daughter I wouldn’t run again.
But then Trump’s chaos came back.
And Lindsey Graham? He cheered.
The truth is, I’m scared. And I’m angry. And I’m done waiting.
So I’m stepping up — because our kids, and this country can’t afford another six years of Lindsey Graham.
I’m building a people-powered campaign to flip South Carolina and give kids the voice they deserve. And I need your help. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
CHIP IN TO STOP MAGA EXTREMISM!>> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
Thank you for believing in this campaign,
Dr. Annie Andrews
